records.name: Haiti
records.summary_text:
Haiti is dangerous for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct is legal, but the national government has effectively collapsed: gangs control most of the capital (Port-au-Prince), the police are outgunned, and mob violence against perceived LGBT people is documented. There is no legal gender recognition, no protection infrastructure, and no functioning judiciary.

The trans-specific risk is inseparable from the generalised collapse — outing in gang-controlled areas can be lethal. A 2018 official US State Department report described attitudes as hostile toward LGBTI individuals who were public

records.name: Fiji
records.summary_text: Fiji is workable for trans visitors — the Pacific islands' leader. Same-sex relations decriminalised in 2010; the 2013 Constitution bans discrimination on the basis of gender identity AND expression — reportedly the only constitution in the world with that explicit pairing. Counterweights: no gender-marker change mechanism, and the Asia Pacific Transgender Network documents high rates of violence and harassment against trans people. Suva has an organised community (Haus of Khameleon, Rainbow Pride Foundation).

records.name: Tonga
records.summary_text: Tonga demands real caution from trans visitors. The Criminal Offences Act criminalises sodomy (10 years, plus corporal punishment on paper — unenforced in recent years) and also criminalises males “impersonating a female” while soliciting — a direct trans-expression statute on the books. Against that: Tonga has a visible leiti (trans-feminine) community with the famous Miss Galaxy pageant (documented by the Washington Post in 2024), family and church networks that are devout but not systematically violent, and no documented recent prosecutions.

records.name: Tuvalu
records.summary_text: Tuvalu demands real caution. Male same-sex conduct criminalised (14 years, unenforced); no LGR; very small, tight-knit, church-centred society; no specifically documented anti-trans violence (population ~11,000). Caveat: very small population — the evidence base is thin, so this assessment carries greater-than-usual uncertainty.

records.name: Solomon Islands
records.summary_text: Solomon Islands is dangerous for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct criminalised (14 years); no LGR; documented social hostility; weak state capacity post-Tensions; no open community infrastructure.

sources.title: LGBTQ rights in Solomon Islands
sources.claim_summary: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer (LGBTQ) people in Solomon Islands face legal challenges not experienced by non-LGBTQ residents. Male and female same-sex sexual activity is illegal, punishable by up to 14 years imprisonment, but the law is not enforced.

records.name: Vanuatu
records.summary_text:
